newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire reports clash with rebels on Lake Tanganyika.
newsitem.headline: Zaire reports clash with rebels on Lake Tanganyika.

text.p: Zaire's defence ministry said on Thursday that government naval units clashed with rebels advancing south in dug-out canoes on Lake Tanganyika in the mineral-rich province of Shaba.
The rebels were advancing towards the port of Moliro around 160 km (100 miles) south of the port of Moba which they captured on Sunday, a spokesman told Reuters.

"Elements of the naval force intercepted the enemy boats. In the clashes that ensued 11 rebels were killed and eight captured including one woman," the spokesman said, adding that rebels used canoes and small boats to capture Kalemie and Moba.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.
The ministry also reported that reinforcements were being sent into to defend the diamond-rich provinces of Kasai.
Shaba and Kasai and copper, diamonds or other minerals mined there are at the heart of Zaire's economy and state revenues.
The ministry said there has been no further news of fighting around the strategic eastern city of Kisangani, headquarters of the Zairean military.
The rebels gave government forces until Thursday to lay down their arms or face an all-out assault on the city.
Earlier, state radio accused Angola of recruiting and training its own fighters to join the rebels.
"These are reinforcements that (rebel leader) Laurent Kabila is waiting for before attacking Kisangani, which is too difficult for the rebels (to take) alone," it said.
Zaire accuses other neighbours Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of invading in support of the rebels. The three countries deny the charges.
